image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a light-colored wooden bookcase filled with books and media cases. The bookcase features multiple horizontal shelves. The left section contains rows of what appear to be CD or DVD cases, while the right section holds hardcover and paperback books. A pair of sunglasses rests on one of the middle-right shelves. The wood grain is visible, and the lighting appears natural, casting soft shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure is clearly a tall, vertical piece of furniture. Although the top and bottom are cropped, the vertical orientation and aspect ratio of the visible frame confirm it is taller than it is wide.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a clear wooden frame with distinct horizontal shelves dividing the space. The geometry is consistent with a standard bookcase frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the front is open and displays items, the bookcase itself is not bilaterally symmetric in this view. It appears to be an L-shaped unit or two adjacent units of different widths/configurations (left side has narrower shelves for CDs, right side has deeper shelves for books). The content arrangement is also asymmetric.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are at least four visible horizontal shelves. They appear to be spaced regularly, though the perspective makes exact measurement difficult. The spacing is functionally even for holding media.
It is impossible to determine if the shelves are adjustable from this static image as no adjustment holes or pins are clearly visible, and the shelves appear fixed into the side panels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are no glass doors visible in the frame. The front is entirely open.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The material is clearly wood with a visible grain pattern and a light finish (likely lacquer or varnish). It does not appear to be particleboard with veneer, but solid wood or high-quality plywood.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shelves are loaded with books, CD/DVD cases, and a pair of sunglasses. The front is unobstructed.

The surfaces are finished (smooth, slight reflection). There is no obvious decorative hardware like knobs or handles, which is typical for open shelving, so the 'finished surfaces' part is present, satisfying the core material requirement.

artifact_observations.location: Spines of books and CD cases on all shelves
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the spines of the books and media cases is illegible and distorted. While some blurring is expected due to resolution and depth of field, the characters do not form recognizable letters or words, exhibiting typical AI-generated 'pseudo-text' artifacts. The patterns resemble text but lack semantic structure.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom-left corner of the bookcase frame
artifact_observations.reasoning: The vertical support on the far left seems to merge ambiguously with the background wall or floor. The line of the bookcase edge becomes soft and indistinct near the bottom crop, suggesting a slight failure in defining the boundary between the object and the environment.

The vertical divider between the left and right sections appears slightly warped or bowed, rather than perfectly straight. This could be lens distortion, but in AI images, it often indicates subtle geometric instability in long vertical lines.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bookcase and not a similar furniture item like a display cabinet or shelving unit, and to verify the material appearance matches wood.
To assess the overall realism, lighting consistency, and texture quality of the wood and books, and to detect any subtle global artifacts.
To rigorously analyze the illegibility of the text on the book and CD spines, confirming if it is gibberish or just out-of-focus real text.
To check for edge bleeding between the bookcase and the wall/background, especially in the lower-left corner where structural collapse was suspected.

focus_areas: Geometric straightness of vertical and horizontal lines
Boundary sharpness between bookcase and background
Consistency of wood grain texture across surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text auditor's findings. If the text is confirmed as gibberish, this is a strong indicator of AI generation despite the realistic overall structure. Also, verify if the 'structural collapse' in the bottom left is a true artifact or just cropping/shadow. The asymmetry of the unit should not be penalized as an error, as L-shaped or mixed-width bookcases exist, but the geometry must be physically plausible.
